content: Butoconazole is a medication prescribed to treat yeast infections of the vagina. It may also be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Butoconazole is available as a cream that is inserted into the vagina. It is typically used once daily at bedtime. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use butoconazole exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or use it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. To use the vaginal cream, follow these steps: 1. Fill the special applicator provided with the cream to the indicated level. 2. Lie on your back with your knees drawn upward and spread apart. 3. Insert the applicator high into your vagina (unless you are pregnant), and then push the plunger to release the medication. If you are pregnant, insert the applicator gently. If you encounter resistance, do not force it further; contact your doctor. 4. Withdraw the applicator and discard it. 5. Wash your hands promptly to prevent spreading the infection. The dose should be applied when you lie down to go to bed. The medication works best if you remain lying down after application, except to wash your hands. You may choose to wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains. Do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using butoconazole even if you feel well, and do not stop using it without consulting your doctor. You should also continue using this medication during your menstrual period. Before using butoconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to butoconazole or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially antibiotics and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had diabetes, immune system problems, HIV infection, or AIDS. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using butoconazole, contact your doctor. If you forget a dose, insert it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not insert a double dose to make up for a missed one. Butoconazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience any of the following symptoms: Burning in the vagina when the cream is inserted Irritation in the vagina when the cream is inserted Stomach pain Fever Foul-smelling discharge If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in the container it came in, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Do not freeze it. Dispose of any outdated or no longer needed medication. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal methods. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Butoconazole is for external use only. Avoid getting the cream in your eyes or mouth, and do not swallow it. Refrain from sexual intercourse while using this medication. An ingredient in the cream may weaken certain latex products, such as condoms or diaphragms, so do not use these products within 72 hours of applying the medication. Wear clean cotton panties (or panties with cotton crotches) rather than those made of nylon, rayon, or other synthetic fabrics. Do not share your medication with others. Ask your pharmacist any questions you have about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the butoconazole treatment, contact your doctor. It is important to keep a written list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, as well as any products such as vitamins, minerals, or dietary supplements. Bring this list with you to every doctor’s visit or if you are admitted to a hospital. This information is also crucial to have in case of emergencies.
